status: bounded mathematical argument and fixed distinguishing witnesses; not general reduction or exhaustive extremizers
proof: Trivial meet and discrete join give a connected simple bipartite block graph with n edges. Its vertex degrees are positive integers with sum 2n and vertex count v<=n+1.
For integer d>=1, phi(d)=d log2(d)>=2(d-1), with equality exactly at d=1,2. For real d>=2 the derivative of phi(d)-2(d-1) is log2(d)+1/ln(2)-2>0; d=1,2 give equality directly.

Under the uniform measure, H(X)=log2(n)-sum_X d log2(d)/n and H(Y)=log2(n)-sum_Y d log2(d)/n. Trivial meet has entropy 0 and discrete join entropy log2(n), so RI=log2(n)-sum_vertices phi(d)/n directly. Thus sum phi(d)>=4n-2v>=2n-2 and RI<=c_n.
Equality requires v=n+1 and every degree in {1,2}: the connected graph is a tree of maximum degree two, hence a path. A path attains c_n since its degrees are two ones and n-1 twos.
